candidate_additions: Assigns Sult2a8 specifically to 7α-hydroxyl bile acid sulfation.
Adds Psmd1-mediated lipid-droplet regulation to the lipid-storage theme.
Adds Car5a-supported ureagenesis and Alad-mediated heme biosynthesis to sulfur/nitrogen metabolism.
Frames the program as periportal/metabolically active.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Drops the explicit Nrf2/CAR co-regulatory interpretation and associated cholestasis-protective mechanism.
Omits Cyp2c50-driven Phase I oxidation from the detoxification module.
Omits Eci2 unsaturated-fatty-acid oxidation and Lonp2 peroxisomal quality control.
Weakens the direct Cdo1–cysteine–gluconeogenesis connection and omits Agmat.
Changes the spatial context from baseline pericentral hepatocytes to candidate periportal hepatocytes.
decision_relevant_differences: The detoxification program is narrowed from coordinated Phase I/II Nrf2/CAR activity to predominantly Phase II sulfation and conjugation.
The lipid axis shifts emphasis from fatty-acid oxidation and peroxisomal maintenance toward lipid-droplet control.
The opposing pericentral versus periportal assignments could affect conclusions about hepatocyte zonation.
assessment.rationale: Both annotations retain the same three central biological themes: bile acid/xenobiotic detoxification, peroxisomal-lipid metabolism, and sulfur metabolism with an aging signature. The candidate adds useful gene-level functions for Sult2a8, Psmd1, Car5a, and Alad, but removes major regulatory and enzymatic details and introduces a conflicting zonation qualifier. These are meaningful refinements and weakenings, not a replacement of the core program interpretation.
shared_core_conclusions: SULT2A enzymes, Gsta3, Akr1c6, and Aldh1a1 define hepatic bile acid/steroid and xenobiotic detoxification.
Hao2, Aldh3a2, and Fitm1 support a peroxisomal/microsomal fatty-acid and lipid-homeostasis axis.
Cdo1 links hepatic cysteine catabolism to taurine, glutathione, and bile-acid metabolism.
Rgn/SMP30 provides an aging-related hepatocyte signature.
The program is connected to hepatic lipid dysregulation in MASLD.
